answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond in the vine ledger and files a sheet of key-signed inputs and outputs. The fable auditor sums all sheets against the pool; a sheet breaking the input-output equation or reusing a receipt burns its bond. The echo checkpoint republishes the total. A single fake risks 105 credits. The k-th filing costs 35+6(k-1): the 1,000th costs 6,029, and 1,000 fakes pay 3,032,000 in fees and lock 70,000 in bonds. A rented-balance ring fails: key-bound receipts mean reuse burns both sheets. An honest agent files once for 35 and recovers its bond if clean.
